1.

Heard Mr. Mohd. Waheed Siddiqui, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Vivek Gupta,
learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.
2. In view of the proposed order, the notice to opposite party No.2 is hereby dispensed with.

3. By means of this anticipatory bail application, the present applicant has prayed for grant of anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.1115 of 2014, under Sections 376/506 I.P.C., Police Station-Hasanganj, District-Unnao.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged in the prosecution story.

5. Attention has been drawn towards Annexure No.12 of the bail application, which is an order dated 11.09.2014, passed by the Division Bench of this Court in Misc. Bench No.8895 of 2014; Ajai (Ajai Kumar) and others vs. State of U.P. & others staying the arrest of the applicant till completion of investigation.

entities.text: Ajai (Ajai Kumar) and others vs. State of U.P. & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The investigation completed and the charge-sheet has been filed against the present applicant.

Challenging the charge-sheet, the present applicant filed a petition bearing Application (U/S 482 Cr.P.C.) No.6480 of 2018; Ajai @ Ajai Kumar vs. State of U.P. and another, which was dismissed by this Court vide order 08.01.2024 (Annexure No.13).

entities.text: Ajai @ Ajai Kumar vs. State of U.P. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that during course of investigation the present applicant cooperated and presently the trial is going on as well as the proceedings of Section 125 Cr.P.C. are pending before the learned Family Court, therefore, the liberty may be protected as he is a government employee.
He has also submitted that in view of the dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case in re: Aman Preet Singh vs. C.B.I. through Director, Criminal Appeal No.929 of 2021.

entities.text: Aman Preet Singh vs. C.B.I. through Director, Criminal Appeal No.929 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Apex Court has observed that in case the charge-sheet has been filed and the applicant was not arrested before filing of the charge-sheet, his arrest could not be warranted after filing of the charge-sheet unless the court concerned has got any specific and cogent reason for taking him into judicial custody.

7. Sri Vivek Gupta, learned Additional Government Advocate has opposed the aforesaid prayer of learned counsel for the applicant by submitting that since this is not a case of false implication and there are, prima-facie, material against the present applicant, therefore, his anticipatory bail application may be rejected.

However, the present applicant may appear/ surrender before the learned trial court raising all pleas and grounds and he may also apprise the learned trial court for his release in the light of the dictum of Apex Court rendered in the case in re: Aman Preet Singh (supra).
8.
Accordingly, having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the material available on record, I find substance in the submission of learned Additional Government Advocate.

9. Therefore, without entering into merits of the issue, I hereby dispose of this application finally at the admission stage giving liberty to the present applicant to appear/surrender before the learned trial court concerned within two weeks from today and file appropriate application taking all pleas and grounds which are available with him including the benefit of dictum of Apex Court rendered in the case in re:Aman Preet Singh (supra) and if the present applicant appears/ surrenders before the learned trial court concerned within the aforesaid stipulated time and files appropriate application,
the same may be decided with expedition, strictly in accordance with law by affording an opportunity of hearing to the parties concerned and without giving any unnecessary adjournment to any of the parties.
10. Since the dictum rendered in the case in re:Aman Preet Singh (supra) is the judgment of Apex Court, therefore, the direction of Apex Court may not be taken into lightly.
